tasks.title: Plan-validation: require a wiring oracle for module-creating leaves
acceptance_criteria: validate_plan emits a 'missing_wiring_oracle' violation for a module-creating leaf whose verification_command names no *_wired oracle
no such violation when the leaf declares a *_wired oracle
no such violation for a pure-edit (refactor) leaf
all existing plan_validator tests still pass
tasks.objective: Add a 'missing_wiring_oracle' plan-validation violation so a leaf that creates a new module is rejected pre-spawn unless it declares a wiring oracle (a *_wired test named in its verification_command).

spec.objective: Add a 'missing_wiring_oracle' plan-validation violation so a leaf that creates a new module is rejected pre-spawn unless it declares a wiring oracle (a *_wired test named in its verification_command).
functional_requirements: In the per-task validation loop of validate_plan, emit a PlanViolation with code 'missing_wiring_oracle' for any MODULE-CREATING leaf whose verification_command does not reference a wiring oracle.

A leaf is MODULE-CREATING when its files_touched contains a .py path that is NOT under a tests/ directory AND its meta_task_type is not a pure-edit type (treat 'refactor', 'logging_observability', and 'docs_writing' and any 'test_*' type as exempt / not module-creating).
A wiring oracle is recognised when the leaf's verification_command names a pytest path whose filename stem ends with '_wired' (e.g. tests/harness/test_newmod_wired.py).
Do not emit the violation when the leaf is not module-creating, or when it already references a *_wired oracle.
Preserve every existing violation and behaviour of validate_plan.
spec.interfaces: A new module-creating/wiring-oracle check inside validate_plan's per-task loop that appends PlanViolation('missing_wiring_oracle', f'{path_prefix}.verification_command', <message>) when required. May add a small module-level helper _is_wiring_oracle(verification_command) -> bool and/or _is_module_creating(task) -> bool. PlanViolation(code, path, message, severity='error') is the existing dataclass.
edge_cases: A 'refactor' leaf touching an existing .py is exempt -- no missing_wiring_oracle violation.
A module-creating leaf whose verification_command references a *_wired oracle passes (no violation).
A leaf whose files_touched are all under tests/ is not module-creating.
non_goals: No change to harness.wire_up, the orchestrator, the overseer gates, or any runtime accept path -- this is the plan-time check only.
No reimplementation of the existing validate_plan; add the new check beside the existing per-task checks (e.g. just after the test_authoring/mutation_target block).
This is an integration edit to an existing module that must preserve all current validation behaviour and tests.
spec.implementation_notes: EDIT the EXISTING file harness/planner/plan_validator.py (it is staged in inbox/targets so you can read its current structure). Inside validate_plan, the per-task loop iterates `for i, task in enumerate(tasks):` building `path_prefix` and appending PlanViolation(...) entries; there is already a block handling meta_task_type == 'test_authoring' that appends mutation-target violations. ADD your new check in that same loop, right AFTER the test_authoring block. Logic: determine module-creating via files_touched (any str path ending '.py' and not containing a 'tests/' segment) AND meta_task_type not in {'refactor','logging_observability','docs_writing'} and not starting with 'test_'; determine wiring-oracle-present by scanning the task's verification_command string for a whitespace token that ends with '.py' whose filename stem ends with '_wired'. When module-creating AND no wiring oracle present, append PlanViolation('missing_wiring_oracle', f'{path_prefix}.verification_command', "a leaf that creates a new module must declare a wiring oracle (a *_wired test named in its verification_command) so the module is proven reachable from a live importer"). You MAY add module-level helpers _is_wiring_oracle(vcmd) and _is_module_creating(task). PlanViolation is the existing frozen dataclass with fields code, path, message, severity='error'. Do NOT change any existing violation. The committed oracle below is authoritative -- your code MUST make it pass while keeping the existing plan_validator tests green.

unit_tests: new module without wiring oracle rejected
new module with wiring oracle passes
regression_tests: new module without wiring oracle -> missing_wiring_oracle
test_spec.test_data_requirements: Plan dicts with single tasks supplied by the committed oracle. integration: this edit preserves existing validate_plan behaviour.
